# src/Connector.Infrastructure

## Overview 🤖

Manages infrastructure components for the connector, including API key authentication, app setting encryption, audit logging, and dynamic export services.

**Responsibilities.** Manages API key authentication, encrypts app settings, logs audit events, and handles dynamic export operations.

| [ExportLogDbContext](#exportlogdbcontext) | dbcontext | 67 | EF Core DbContext for the export log (SQLite). Tables: ExportRun, AppSetting (key/value config store), AuditLog. | [DynamicExportService](#dynamicexportservice) | service | 18 | Query/build engine behind the connector's export paths: the legacy single-mapping flat/nested-JSON pipeline (`ExportMappingConfig`, still served by /api/pipeline/* — see DynamicExportService.LegacyMapping.cs) and the `ExportNode` tree engine (Export Definitions 2.0 — see DynamicExportService.ExportNode.cs) side by side, plus the shared GDPR denylist (DynamicExportService.Gdpr.cs) and output-format writers (DynamicExportService.Output.cs) both paths use. Kept as one partial class split across files by responsibility, rather than separate classes, so every existing DynamicExportService.* call site across the API/Infrastructure/test projects keeps working unchanged. This file holds the members shared across every other part: the nesting-depth cap, the build-result shape, the connection fingerprint, and the dialect lookup both query engines build on. |
| [ErrorSanitizer](#errorsanitizer) | class | 17 | Strips credentials from error text. Several endpoints return an exception's message to the caller (a "test connection"/preview action is only useful if it says why it failed), but Npgsql can echo the offending connection string — including the ERP password — back inside an exception message. `Detail` is the single choke point every such call site routes through, so the diagnostic value survives but a credential can't leak through it. `ForLogging` does the same for logged exceptions, and `Scrub` for any other text such as audit details. |
| [UserStore](#userstore) | class | 6 | Lookup and seeding helpers over `Users`. |
| [ExportDefinitionEntity](#exportdefinitionentity) | entity | 4 | One saved, independently named and scheduled export: a name, the table it's rooted at, its `ExportNode` tree, and the output format/schedule it runs with. Replaces the single AppSetting-backed mapping + presets (`ExportMapping`/`ExportPresets`). |
| [ExportDefinitionRunner](#exportdefinitionrunner) | class | 4 | The one execution path behind every trigger of an `ExportDefinitionEntity` — manual run/test (ExportDefinitionEndpoints) and scheduled runs (`ExportDefinitionWorker`) all call `ExecuteAsync`, so every run — scheduled or manual — writes exactly one `ExportDefinitionRunEntity` row, with identical Failed/error-message semantics regardless of trigger. |

## Components

### ApiKeyStore

_class_ · [ApiKeyStore.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/ApiKeyStore.cs#L14)

Machine-to-machine credential check for endpoints a "dedicated API user" calls directly (no interactive login) — e.g. an external system triggering a saved export preset. Deliberately not BCrypt: a BCrypt verify is intentionally slow (work-factor tuned to resist brute-forcing a human-chosen password) and this runs on every single request rather than once at login, while a generated API key is already high-entropy, so a fast, constant-time SHA-256 comparison is the appropriate trade-off here. Never stores or compares the raw key — only its hash, both at rest (config) and in memory.

_Linked tests:_ `ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_MatchingKey_ReturnsTrueWithConfiguredName`, `ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_MultipleConfiguredKeys_MatchesTheRightOne`, `ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_NoConfiguredKeys_ReturnsFalse`, `ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_WrongKey_ReturnsFalse`, `ApiKeyStoreTests.Hash_SameInput_IsDeterministicAndLowercaseHex` (via `ApiKeyStore.Hash(string)`) — test code that uses it, not coverage

### AppSettingEncryptionMigrator

_class_ · [AppSettingEncryptionMigrator.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/AppSettingEncryptionMigrator.cs#L16)

One-time, idempotent startup step that encrypts every AppSetting.Value still stored as plaintext — rows written before `EncryptedStringConverter` existed. The converter only encrypts a row when it is saved again, and several keys (e.g. scheduler_config, read on every worker tick) are rarely re-saved, so without this they would stay plaintext on disk indefinitely and trigger the converter's plaintext warning on every single read.

_Linked tests:_ `AppSettingEncryptionTests.Migrator_EncryptsPlaintextRows_LeavesCiphertextAlone_AndIsIdempotent` (via `AppSettingEncryptionMigrator.EncryptPlaintextRowsAsync(ExportLogDbContext, IDataProtectionProvider, ILogger, CancellationToken)`) — test code that uses it, not coverage

### CronSchedule

_class_ · [CronSchedule.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/CronSchedule.cs#L9)

Minimal 5-field cron matcher (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, UTC) for `Schedule`. Not a general cron library: no seconds field, no `L`/`W`/`#` extensions — only what the UI's Manual/Hourly/Daily/Weekly presets plus a free-text advanced field can produce. The matching logic is a few dozen lines, so no scheduling library is used.

| [`ExecuteExportNodeQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider, Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, string, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode, System.Threading.CancellationToken, int?, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet<string>?, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection?)`](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/DynamicExportService.ExportNode.cs#L103) ⚠ | Runs one `ExportNode` tree (rooted at `rootTable`) and returns one JSON tree per root row — the generic successor to `ExecuteNestedJsonQueryAsync` that also covers plain scalar columns, so it is the only query path `BuildExportNodeAsync` needs regardless of output format. The database returns plain rows, one query per tree node; the tree is assembled in C# (`ExecuteTreeQueryAsync`). Every scalar is a JSON string of its ::text form (or JSON null), an array node with no matches is [], an object node with no match is null, and an object node with several matches fails the export. GDPR enforcement is two layers: a denylisted `SourceField` is excluded from the SELECT list entirely (so it never leaves the database, and — since this is re-evaluated against the *current* denylist on every run — a definition saved before a field was denylisted is covered too, not just newly-saved ones), plus `StripGdprFieldsRecursive`'s output-key match as a second, independent layer of defence-in-depth. | dependencies: none; side effects (inferred): db | 6 |

### EncryptedStringConverter

_class_ · [EncryptedStringConverter.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/EncryptedStringConverter.cs#L20)

Encrypts a string column at rest via ASP.NET Core Data Protection. Applied to `Value`, which stores the ERP connection config including its password, so a stolen backup or disk snapshot of the SQLite file doesn't expose it. EF Core runs the conversion on every SaveChanges/materialization, so every caller — `AppSettingsStore`'s helpers and the several call sites that read `AppSettings` directly — keeps seeing plaintext JSON; only the bytes actually persisted to disk are ciphertext.

### ErrorSanitizer

_class_ · [ErrorSanitizer.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/ErrorSanitizer.cs#L13)

Strips credentials from error text. Several endpoints return an exception's message to the caller (a "test connection"/preview action is only useful if it says why it failed), but Npgsql can echo the offending connection string — including the ERP password — back inside an exception message. `Detail` is the single choke point every such call site routes through, so the diagnostic value survives but a credential can't leak through it. `ForLogging` does the same for logged exceptions, and `Scrub` for any other text such as audit details.

### ImportNodeWalker

_class_ · [ImportNodeWalker.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/ImportNodeWalker.cs#L18)

The write-side mirror of `DynamicExportService`'s tree walker: parses an inbound ImportEnvelope against a saved `ImportNode` tree, and produces a field-level diff per accepted row plus a rejected-row list — with zero write capability. ### ImportWorker

_class_ · [ImportWorker.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/ImportWorker.cs#L29)

A sibling of `ExportWorker` that polls an inbound/ staging folder instead of writing to one. Every vendor-supplied file dropped there is manifest-checked, idempotency-checked against (ImportDefinitionId, Sha256Checksum), walked by `ImportNodeWalker` against the ImportEnvelope — the definition field says which saved `ImportDefinitionEntity` to use — and staged as an `ImportRunEntity` at `PendingReview`, with `ImportDefinitionEntity` frozen onto it as `DefinitionSnapshotJson`. This worker never writes to the ERP itself — that's `ImportRunReleaser`'s job, once a human approves the staged plan.

### SessionRevocationStore

_class_ · [SessionRevocationStore.cs](../../src/Connector.Infrastructure/SessionRevocationStore.cs#L12)

JWT revocation: stores, per username, the earliest a JWT for that user may have been issued to still be considered valid. Every token carries its own issued-at claim (see AuthEndpoints), and Program.cs's OnTokenValidated handler rejects any token issued before that cutover. Backed by the encrypted-at-rest `AppSettingEntity` key/value store rather than a dedicated table. Self-service only: a user can revoke their own sessions (POST /api/auth/revoke-my-sessions). There is no admin action to revoke another user's sessions, since there is no role model to authorize it.
